# vawe: one JSON scene -> one deterministic video

## About vawe

vawe turns one self-describing JSON scene into a deterministic 30fps mp4. Every video is one JSON
file: `"module": "scene"` at the top, then a theme, a duration, a moving background, and a list of
layers. The renderer calls `renderFrame(n)` for every frame; nothing runs live, nothing drifts, the
same JSON always produces the same pixels. There are five canvases (16:9, 9:16, 1:1, 4:5, 4:3); an
aspect not named here still renders, sized to fit the long edge at 1920.

There is exactly one module. There are no templates: you compose a film from a vocabulary of layer
types plus effects that apply to them (motion, colour, transitions, sound), the same way you compose a
sentence from words, not from a form.

## Project structure: the minimal runnable scene

Every scene needs `module`, `theme`, `duration`, a `bg` (the backdrop MUST be declared, and should
move across the runtime, not sit static), and `layers` (at least one). This is the smallest real one:

```json
{
  "module": "scene",
  "theme": "default",
  "duration": 6,
  "bg": [
    { "from": 0, "to": 3, "preset": "soft" },
    { "from": 3, "to": 6, "preset": "accent" }
  ],
  "layers": [
    {
      "type": "text",
      "text": "One data point beats a slide of ten",
      "x": 100, "y": 420, "w": 880, "size": 84, "weight": 800,
      "split": "word", "preset": "blurUp",
      "start": 0.2, "duration": 2.4
    }
  ]
}
```

## The vocabulary: layer types

Every layer's `type` is one of these 24 (pulled live from the layer registry, so this list
cannot go stale). Everything else in the vocabulary below is a dial ON one of these.

- `text`: theme-styled words in an optional chip box, auto-fit to a width; the typewriter reveal and caret live here too; `typingColors` flashes each word its own accent colour the instant it types, then settles to ink WHEN: the default for any on-screen word or line; reach for it before any other layer for copy.
- `count`: a number that counts from -> to across its own window, formatted (compacts at 1e6, prefix/suffix/decimals). The text build plus a per-frame value. `roll: true` makes it an ODOMETER: one masked wheel per digit, each sliding to its next value, geared so a wheel only turns as the wheel below it crosses 9 WHEN: a claim IS a number; use this instead of typing the number into a `text` layer.
- `image`: an <img> with cover-fit, radius, a ken-burns slow zoom and an edge dissolve; `canvasFx` bakes a per-pixel pass into it at boot WHEN: a real picture exists (a photo, a capture, a screenshot); prefer it over `html` or a drawn icon.
- `video`: real footage, SEEKED to a computed source time every frame and never played, so the picture is as deterministic as a still WHEN: real footage exists and the beat needs it to move; still deterministic, never "played".
- `group`: layout by containment: a flex/grid box whose children (any depth) flow with a gap, so a card + label + chip can never desync WHEN: two or more layers must move and stay aligned together (a card + its label + its chip).
- `rect`: a plain box, panel, card or pill. it carries no text: put that on a higher track WHEN: a plain box, panel, divider or accent bar with no text of its own.
- `glow`: soft light with no WebGL: a radial centre glow, a directional beam, or a named phenomenon (bloom · halation · diffusion · rimLight · spotlight) WHEN: a light source or a soft halo is the point of the layer, not a decoration on top of one.
- `beam`: a light that travels the rounded-rect border, or a sheen that sweeps across the box; the travel is closed-form in t, not a CSS keyframe WHEN: light travelling a border or sweeping a box; the traced-outline look no CSS animation can seek.
- `svg`: a vector mark that DRAWS itself on (stroke dashoffset) and then RESOLVES INTO ITS FILL, the stroke leaving as the solid logo arrives, or MELTS from one path into another (true point-lerp morph, optional spin) WHEN: a vector mark (a logo, an icon path) that should draw itself on or morph, not just fade in.
- `cursor`: a pointer that follows [{t,x,y}] keyframes (`path`) or eases magnetically onto another layer's live box (`snapTo`), fires a ripple at `clicks`, can change shape mid-move (`style`/`styleAt`: arrow/hand/ibeam/block), carry a name tag (`label`), and drag another layer along with it (`carry`) WHEN: the beat IS a product demo; this is the one primitive built to drive a click-through.
- `clip`: a video played as a preloaded PNG frame sequence: the frame swaps the <img> src, so no decoder state can drift between renders WHEN: footage came in as a frame sequence (PNG/WebP), not a video file, and must stay seek-exact.
- `html`: raw hand-authored HTML/CSS as ONE layer, still positioned and animated by the engine; <script> is stripped and CSS transition/animation refused, use `parts` to give its pieces the clock WHEN: the surface does not exist yet and CSS genuinely expresses it faster than composing primitives; see engine-doctrine/CRAFT/HTML-FRAGMENTS.md before hand-writing one.
- `component`: a REAL captured UI block (`make capture`), or one named part of a captured scene, scaled to fit `w` WHEN: a real product surface was captured (`make capture`); always prefer this over `html` when the surface actually exists.
- `board`: a populated workspace from pure data: up to 4 columns of up to 5 mini issue-cards, entering as one clip WHEN: the beat is "here is our roadmap/backlog" from pure data, no captured asset needed.
- `doc`: a file card from pure data: an optional filename + diff chip, then heading / body / code / bullet blocks, theme-styled and auto-height WHEN: the beat is "here is a file/diff/README" from pure data, no captured asset needed.
- `shader`: a full-frame generative WebGL field (see the ambient shaders), pure in t and palette-tintable; it carries no sampler, so it cannot read what is beneath it. `shaderKeys` cycles ONE panel through several looks on hard cuts, in one context, instead of stacking a layer per look WHEN: the whole frame is a generative backdrop; it cannot sample what is beneath it.
- `lottie`: an After Effects (Bodymovin) export driven by ABSOLUTE seek, goToAndStop at a frame index, never autoplay WHEN: a Bodymovin/After Effects export already exists; it is seeked, never autoplayed.
- `paint`: a generative Canvas 2D field drawn per frame from local time. The canvas family written in JS rather than GLSL, and the one you can resample WHEN: a generative field is needed AND it must be resampled as a texture by another layer.
- `raymarch`: a lit implicit surface from a distance field: a camera, a normal and a silhouette. the most expensive primitive in the engine. One hero shot, sized to what it needs WHEN: one hero 3D shot justifies the most expensive primitive in the engine; never for a whole film.
- `three`: a real three.js scene graph (meshes, materials, lights, a camera) posed absolutely from t, for what a distance field cannot express: a font outline, a device body, a captured UI plane, a point cloud WHEN: a real geometry (a font extrusion, a device body, a captured UI plane) is needed, not just a field.
- `globe`: a dotted planet with tapered route arcs, drawn by vendored cobe: atmospheric glow and a diffuse terminator. reach for `three:"globe"` instead only when you need a real sun vector WHEN: a dotted-planet-with-routes beat; reach for `three:"globe"` only when a real sun vector matters.
- `particles`: a deterministic particle emitter: `preset` picks confetti (a gravity-fed burst), sparks (a fast radial flash) or dust (a slow ambient drift). Closed-form per particle, seeded by `seed`, never a running sim WHEN: a burst, flash or drift of many identical small marks (confetti/sparks/dust), deterministic.
- `composition`: names a first-party hand-authored GSAP timeline in core/compositions/ and passes it DATA; for choreography `parts` and recipes cannot express WHEN: the beat needs bespoke first-party choreography that `parts` and recipes cannot express.
- `adjust`: one grade over everything BENEATH it: blur, desaturate, darken, brighten or contrast the whole frame from a single layer, keyable through `vars` on `--adjust` WHEN: grade everything BENEATH one point in the stack (blur/darken/desaturate a whole background).

Full props per type: `films/scene/schema.json`. What each type is FOR, in prose: `engine-doctrine/PRIMITIVES.md`.

## The vocabulary: effect families

Do not try to memorise all 926 named things the engine can do; reach for them by family, then
search within the family. Each of these 58 families is a dial you put ON a layer, a cut,
the camera, or the scene:

- **Drawn icons** (16, `asset`): `svgIcon("<name>")`: a first-party vector, when no real logo or captured UI exists.
- **Motion voices (tactile sound)** (6, `audio`): The film SOUNDS its own motion.
- **Backgrounds** (23, `background`): `bg:[{preset,from,to}]`.
- **Gradient recipes** (24, `background`): named colour+kind(+angle) combos for the `gradient` background preset: `{"preset":"gradient","opts":{"recipe":"NAME"}}`.
- **Camera dials** (1, `camera`): Top-level scene keys that change what the camera DOES rather than where it goes.
- **Camera moves** (15, `camera`): `"cameraMove": { "move":"<name>", ...
- **Destinations (platform safe area)** (6, `canvas`): `"destination": "<name>"`.
- **Output targets** (5, `canvas`): `aspect` picks the CANVAS.
- **Caption styles** (19, `captions`): `captionStyle:"<name>"` alongside a `captions:[{t0,t1,text}]` array.
- **Compositions (bespoke per-beat timeline)** (2, `composition`): `{ "type":"composition", "comp":"<name>", "props":{…} }`.
- **Cut timings** (9, `cuts[]/per-layer`): The SPEED CURVE a cut travels on, chosen separately from the cut itself: `cuts:[{ "t":3, "style":"push", "timing":"ramp" }]`, or `cutTiming` on a per-layer cut.
- **Generators (the playground)** (8, `generator`): Parametric field generators with declared option schemas, turnable at /playground and usable as a `bg` or a layer.
- **Lightfield envelope anchors** (2, `generator`): Which edge an element grows FROM.
- **Lightfield envelope shapes** (9, `generator`): How an element's extent varies with where it sits, as a curve across the row.
- **Lightfield motions** (4, `generator`): How the field lives against the frame clock.
- **Lightfield patterns** (3, `generator`): The STRUCTURE of a lightfield: what the elements are and which way the eye travels across them.
- **Lightfield shadow directions** (11, `generator`): Which way "away" is: the bearing the light falls off along.
- **Glow presets** (7, `glow layer`): `preset` on a `glow` layer, the same slot the kinetic presets use on a text layer and a different vocabulary, because a glow carries no split text.
- **Raymarched surfaces** (6, `layer`): `{ "type":"raymarch", "raymarch":"<name>" }`.
- **three.js scenes (real geometry)** (12, `layer`): `{ "type":"three", "three":"<name>" }`.
- **Interpolation modes (not easings)** (1, `motion key`): On a `motion` key's `ease`, but NOT a curve.
- **Keyframe handles (the graph editor)** (5, `motion key`): On a `motion` or `camera` key, per SIDE: `easeOut` shapes the segment LEAVING the key, `easeIn` the segment ARRIVING at it, so one segment is drawn by two handles.
- **Particles presets** (3, `particles layer`): `preset` on a `particles` layer picks the emitter: `{ "type":"particles", "preset":"confetti" }`.
- **Ambient shader fields** (27, `per-frame`): `{ "type":"shader", "shader":"<name>" }`.
- **Generative paint FX (per-frame)** (5, `per-frame`): `{ "type":"paint", "paint":"<name>" }`.
- **Layer-as-texture (resample)** (9, `per-frame`): `"resample":{ "fx":"<name>", "amount":[from,to] }`.
- **Adjustment layers (grade what is BENEATH)** (6, `per-layer`): `{ "type":"adjust", "kind":"<name>" }`.
- **Blend modes** (17, `per-layer`): `mixBlend`: how a layer composites with what is already painted beneath it.
- **Cursor styles** (4, `per-layer`): What shape a `cursor` layer draws (`"style": "hand"`), and how it can change mid-move (`styleAt`).
- **Depths (parallax planes)** (4, `per-layer`): `{ "depth": "back" }` on any layer.
- **Effector drives** (6, `per-layer`): What an effector's influence is SPENT on: `drives: { scale: 0.6, push: 90 }`, where the number is the amount at full influence.
- **Effector falloffs** (4, `per-layer`): A FALLOFF FROM A TRAVELLING POINT, driving the layer's own children.
- **Enter / exit anims** (19, `per-layer`): `anim` (enter) + `out` (exit) on any layer.
- **Move shapes (measured keyframe tracks)** (5, `per-layer`): A storyboard's `move: <shape>:<band>` (harness/lib/contract.mjs, scope LAYER: a sustained track on the beat's own layer, never a one-shot entrance), or a hand-keyed `motion` built directly: `node harness/author/track.mjs pan --dur 1.25 --to -600`.
- **Part entrances** (9, `per-layer`): THE BRIDGE between hand-written markup and the engine's clock.
- **Path curves (SVG "d" generators)** (4, `per-layer`): A storyboard's `move: <curve>:<band>` (harness/lib/contract.mjs, scope PATH: flies the beat's own layer along the curve, MotionPathPlugin), or `modifiers: [{ alongPath: { curve } }]` (core/fx/along-path.js) to set a line of type on it instead of moving a whole layer.
- **Per-layer modifiers** (14, `per-layer`): `"modifiers"` on a layer, applied in array order after every motion track.
- **Idles (ambient hold motion)** (3, `per-layer/scene`): `idle` on a layer, or scene-level `idle` for the whole cast.
- **GSAP named effects** (30, `per-layer/text`): `fx` on a layer, pair with `anim:"none"` so GSAP owns the transform.
- **Placement** (20, `pin`): `"pin": "<name>"` on a layer or a caption.
- **Spectacle devices** (12, `scene`): `"spectacle": { "at", "of", "device", "why" }`.
- **Canvas image passes (baked)** (8, `static`): `canvasFx`: a one-time baked image pass (cannot move).
- **Composite looks (static)** (31, `static`): `filter:"<look>"`.
- **Filter presets** (15, `static`): `filter:"<name>"`.
- **Kinetic text presets** (33, `text`): `split`+`preset` on a text layer.
- **Ransom faces** (8, `text`): `ransom` on a text layer: per-glyph face mixing, from this fixed set.
- **Scramble charsets (`chars`)** (7, `text`): What `preset: "decode"` scrambles WITH, in `presetOpts`: `{ "preset":"decode", "presetOpts": { "chars":"numbers", "rate":48, "revealDelay":0.25 } }`.
- **Font-variation axes** (4, `text track`): A variable face moves inside the letters: an `axis` track ramps one axis per unit on the same stagger clock as `preset`.
- **Stagger order (`from`)** (6, `text/parts`): The ORDER a stagger runs in, on `stagger` as an object: `{ "stagger": { "amount": 0.6, "from": "center" } }`.
- **Theme look keys** (6, `theme`): A theme (`themes/<name>.json`) may carry a `look` block: the whole-film default a brand fixes so a scaffold does not re-decide it per video (engine-doctrine/CRAFT/THEME-LOOK.md).
- **Easings** (46, `timing`): `ease` on a motion key, a count, a camera leg.
- **Group clock loop shapes** (2, `timing`): The `loop` field of a group's `clock`.
- **Time remaps (the layer's own clock)** (4, `timing`): `timeRemap` on a layer.
- **Film energy** (4, `top-level`): One word at the top of the scene sets the default speed curve for every cut and seam that names no `timing`.
- **Scene cuts** (27, `transition`): `cuts:[{t,style}]`.
- **Seams (2-scene blends)** (26, `transition`): `seams:[{t,fx,dur}]`.
- **Shader stings** (35, `transition`): `stings:[{t,fx}]`.
- **Transition relationships** (9, `transition`): Name the RELATIONSHIP between two beats first, then pick from its candidates, per engine-doctrine/CRAFT/TRANSITIONS.md's decision procedure.

**Discovery, not memorisation:** `make arsenal Q="a page scrolling under a static tilt"` searches all
926 named things (layer types, every family above, recipes, blocks, sound cues) by plain-English
description and returns the exact key to write. `make arsenal AT="layers[].motion[]"` answers the other
half: what fields are legal to write at one JSON path, read live off `films/scene/schema.json`.

## The hard rules

- No em-dash (U+2014) in any on-screen text; the validator rejects it. Use a comma, a period, or middle dot.
- First-frame hook: 12 words or fewer, the strong word first, at most one emoji.
- `bg` is required, and it should MOVE. A static field is a decision you must be able to defend, never a default.
- Author the motion, do not name it: a hand-keyed `motion` track on the layer that carries the film's
  one loud beat reads as directed; a preset reads as decorated. Reserve presets for everything else.
- Hold the film across its cuts with a real device: a continuous object (one layer that survives a cut
  and changes across it) or a declared alternative (a motif, a match cut, a sound bridge) named in a
  waiver's `_why`. A film with neither is a slideshow, not a film.
- Show, do not only tell: a beat that makes a claim should be asked what it could SHOW (a real captured
  UI, a counted number, a real chart) before it is set only in type.

## The loop

```
make pitch                          # ask the four questions: subject, data, payoff, audience/feeling
                                     # write films/scene/x.storyboard.md from engine-doctrine/CRAFT/STORYBOARD-TEMPLATE.md
make dev D=films/scene/x.json     # THE iteration loop: build, draft-render, look. No gates.
make ship D=films/scene/x.json    # the real ladder: author-check -> render -> audit -> seams
make judge D=films/scene/x.json   # the one step that SEES: composition and fidelity, post-render
```

## Discovery

- `make arsenal Q="<what you mean, in plain english>"` searches all 926 named things at once and
  prints the JSON key that means it.
- `make arsenal AT="<json path>"` answers what is legal to write at that path, with every field's type.
- `make list` shows the scene module's schema and a sample scene end to end.
